title: Migrate chart theme tokens to CSS variables and accessibility hydration
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need to standardize chart visual tokens by migrating the current JS-based token surface to CSS custom properties (CSS vars) and introduce a lightweight runtime hydration toggle for accessibility testing. Current problems: (1) theme tokens for charts live in multiple places (component-level JS, hard-coded chart renderer values, and legacy CSS fallbacks) which makes small visual updates error-prone; (2) runtime theme switches cause full re-mounts of chart canvases increasing perceived latency; (3) accessibility QA requires toggling high-contrast and reduced-motion variants without large perf regressions. This ticket covers design decisions, token naming conventions, migration strategy, and a controlled rollout for charts (time-series, sparkline, bandline) to use CSS variables exposed by the design system, plus a minimal JS hydration layer that maps tokens into renderer configuration only when necessary (e.g., high-contrast mode or user-selected palette). Goals: reduce DOM/JS churn during theme changes, make tokens consumable by non-React surfaces (raw canvas renderers), improve the team's ability to ship color updates with minimal risk, and provide a11y toggle with predictable performance.
acceptance_criteria: Chart color, spacing, and typography tokens are defined as CSS custom properties and documented in the design system tokens page
Renderer can read fallback values from CSS vars without requiring a full component remount
High-contrast and reduced-motion modes can be toggled at runtime with <100ms median impact on first-paint for charts under representative load
Unit and visual regression tests updated to reference token names instead of hard-coded hex values
Design token migration PR merged and release notes added to design-system-1.12
tasks: Audit current chart token locations (component JS, renderer defaults, legacy CSS) and produce mapping table
Propose canonical token namespace and names (chart-*) and publish in tokens spec
Create CSS var shim that maps existing theme tokens to new CSS vars for backwards compatibility
Implement renderer read-path: prefer CSS var lookup, fallback to current JS token if var not present
Add a11y runtime hydration toggle to only reconfigure renderer when an a11y preference changes
Measure perf: baseline current mount/hydration, measure after CSS var approach, record p95/p50 latency
Update Figma tokens and export snippets for engineers
Ship a canary build behind feature flag and coordinate with front-end infra for rollout
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Chen: Created ticket after cross-team design sync. Noted inconsistencies in chart palette across time-series and minimap components.
2026-02-24 Alejandro Ruiz: Completed initial audit. Found 27 unique color references across 12 chart modules. Uploaded mapping spreadsheet to Drive: https://drive.redwood.dev/design/chart-token-audit
2026-02-28 Design review: Decided on token prefix --chart- and variants like --chart-line, --chart-fill-muted. Will avoid semantic-only tokens for urgent rollout to reduce consumer changes.

2026-03-03 Engineering feedback (Kenji Patel): Proposed renderer CSS var read-path; warned about computedStyle cost when reading individual properties for thousands of points. Plan: read computedStyle once per renderer instance and cache values in renderer config.
2026-03-06 Performance note (R&D): Micro-benchmarks show computedStyle read is ~0.9ms per property first-read, but subsequent reads are cheap when cached. We'll batch reads and memoize per-theme.
2026-03-09 Accessibility QA (Zoe Martin): Verified the high-contrast token set in a prototype. Minor contrast tweaks required for bandline fill at small opacities. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-10 Alejandro Ruiz: Opened PR for token definitions and CSS var shim: https://github.com/redwoodinference/design-system/pull/874. CI failing on two visual snapshots — investigating difference in label weights when using CSS vars in canvas text rendering.
